The first season of the American [[television program|television]] [[comedy]] ''[[The Office (American TV series)|The Office]]'' premiered in the United States on [[NBC]] on March 24, 2005, concluded on April 26, 2005, and consists of six episodes.  ''The Office'' is an American adaptation of the [[The Office (British TV series)|British TV series]], and is presented in a [[mockumentary]] format, portraying the daily lives of office employees in the [[Scranton, Pennsylvania]] branch of the fictitious [[Dunder Mifflin|Dunder Mifflin Paper Company]]. The season stars [[Steve Carell]], [[Rainn Wilson]], [[John Krasinski]], [[Jenna Fischer]], and [[B. J. Novak]].

This season introduced the main characters, and established the general plot, which revolves around [[Michael Scott (The Office)|Michael Scott]] (Carell), regional manager of the Scranton branch office, trying to convince the filmmakers of the documentary that he presides over a happy, well-running office. Meanwhile, sales rep [[Jim Halpert]] (Krasinski) finds methods to undermine his cube-mate, [[Dwight Schrute]] (Wilson); receptionist [[Pam Beesly]] (Fischer) tries to deal with Michael's insensitivities and flubs; and temporary employee [[Ryan Howard (The Office)|Ryan Howard]] (Novak) is acting mostly as an observer of the insanity around him.

The first season of ''The Office'' aired on Tuesdays in the United States at 9:30&nbsp;p.m. The season debuted to high numbers and garnered moderately positive reviews from critics, aside from the pilot, which received mixed reviews. While some enjoyed the pilot, others opined that it was a mere copy of the original British version. [[Universal Studios Home Entertainment]] released the season in a single DVD on August 16, 2005. The DVD contained all six episodes, along with commentaries from creators, writers, actors, and directors on most of the episodes, as well as deleted scenes from all of the episodes.

==Production==
The first season of the show was produced by [[Reveille Productions]] and Deedle-Dee Productions, both in association with [[NBC Universal Television Studio]]s.<ref name=credits>{{cite AV media notes |title=The Office: The Complete First Season |last=Kwapis|first=Ken|type=DVD |publisher=[[NBC]]|display-authors=etal|year=2005}}</ref> The show is based on the [[The Office (British TV series)|British comedy series of the same name]], which was created by [[Ricky Gervais]] and [[Stephen Merchant]] for the British Broadcasting Corporation ([[BBC]]).<ref name=office-original/><ref name="GreenLight">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2004/may/18/broadcasting.internationalnews|title=American Office Gets Green Light|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=December 18, 2025}}</ref> This season was produced by [[Greg Daniels]], along with consulting producers [[Larry Wilmore]] and [[Lester Lewis]].<ref name=credits/><ref>{{cite web|last=Bashir|first=Martin|date=October 10, 2007|url=http://www.abcnews.go.com/Nightline/Story?id=3703737&page=1|title=Veteran TV Writer Moves in Front of the Camera|work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|access-date=March 7, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Adalian|first=Josef|title=WB Finds King of 'Kings'|url=https://www.proquest.com/magazines/nielsen-ratings-report/docview/236226739/se-2?accountid=14556|access-date=January 7, 2026|newspaper=[[Variety (magazine)|Daily Variety]]|date=July 5, 2005}} {{subscription required}}</ref> Writers for the season included Daniels, Gervais, Merchant, Michael Schur, [[Mindy Kaling]], [[Paul Lieberstein]], and [[B. J. Novak]].<ref name=credits/><ref>{{cite web|last=Paumgarten|first=Nick|date=October 3, 2005|url=http://www.newyorker.com/archive/2005/10/03/051003ta_talk_paumgarten|title='Fender Bender'|work=[[The New Yorker]]|access-date=March 7, 2008}}</ref> For this season, Schur was a co-producer, Kaling was a staff writer, Lieberstein was a consulting producer, and Novak was an executive story editor.<ref name=credits/> Though Daniels is credited as a writer for "[[Pilot (The Office)|Pilot]]", the majority of the episode was adapted from "[[Episode One (The Office, Series One)|Downsize]]" of the British series, with many scenes being transferred almost verbatim.<ref name="danielsinterview2">{{cite web|url=https://heywriterboy.blogspot.com/2007/06/in-conversation-greg-daniels-executive.html|title=In Conversation: Greg Daniels, Executive Producer/Showrunner of The Office (U.S.)|publisher=HeyWriterBoy|date=June 20, 2007|access-date=November 13, 2011}}</ref>

The first season featured episodes directed by five different directors: [[Ken Kwapis]] directed "Pilot" and "[[Diversity Day (The Office)|Diversity Day]]", [[Ken Whittingham]] directed "[[Health Care (The Office)|Health Care]]", [[Bryan Gordon]] directed "[[The Alliance (The Office)|The Alliance]]", [[Amy Heckerling]] directed "[[Hot Girl (The Office)|Hot Girl]]", and Daniels both produced and directed "[[Basketball (The Office)|Basketball]]".<ref name=credits/> This season of ''The Office'' was almost entirely filmed in an actual office building in [[Los Angeles California|Los Angeles]], [[California]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Glassman |first=Thea |date=March 19, 2020 |title=How the Remarkably Unremarkable World of Dunder Mifflin Was Built |url=https://www.architecturaldigest.com/story/the-office-anniversary-dunder-mifflin-set-design |access-date=January 6, 2025 |website=Architectural Digest |language=en-US}}</ref> Footage of [[Scranton]], Pennsylvania, taken by John Krasinski was also used in the opening theme.<ref>{{cite web|last=Marchese|first=John|date=October 21, 2005|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/10/21/arts/television/21marc.html?ex=1350619200&en=903ceb28d88bdeb6&ei=5088&partner=rssnyt&emc=rss|title=Scranton Embraces the ''Office'' Infamy|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=December 24, 2025}}</ref>

==Cast==
{{see also|List of The Office (American TV series) characters}}
''The Office'' employed an [[ensemble cast]]. Most of the main characters, and some supporting ones, are based on characters from the British version of ''The Office''. While these characters normally have the same attitudes and perceptions as their British counterparts, the roles have been redesigned to better fit the American show. The show featured a large cast size, many of whom were known for their [[Improvisation|improvisational]] work.<ref name=office-original>{{cite web |last1=Gilbert |first1=Holly |title=The Office US Vs. UK Versions: Differences Explained |url=https://screenrant.com/office-us-vs-uk-versions-differences-explained/ |website=[[Screen Rant]] |access-date=December 18, 2025 |date=November 1, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Fotis|first=Matt|title=Fifty Key Improv Performers: Actors, Troupes, and Schools from Theatre, Film, and TV|publisher=[[Routledge]]|location=[[London]]|isbn=9781040113981|quote=''The Office'' incorporated improv into the show. The talking head interviews almost always featured improvised takes by the cast members, and they filmed many of the scripted scenes multiple times to allow for improvisation.|section=31. Steve Carell and Stephen Colbert}}</ref>

===Main===
* [[Steve Carell]] as [[Michael Scott (The Office)|Michael Scott]], regional manager of the Dunder Mifflin Scranton Branch.<ref>{{cite web|last=Jones|first=Del|date=September 27, 2007|url=https://www.usatoday.com/money/companies/management/2007-09-26-the-office_N.htm|title=Taking 'Office' Lessons from the World's Greatest (Inept) Boss|work=[[USA Today]]|access-date=March 7, 2008}}</ref>  Loosely based on [[David Brent]], Gervais' character in the British version,<ref>{{cite web|last=Stanley|first=Alessandra|date=April 8, 2007|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9800EFD81F30F93BA35757C0A9619C8B63&scp=20&sq=the+office+carell&st=nyt|title=Jolly Good Show Or Was It?; On TV, Attitude Is More Important Than the Way the Vowels Sound|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=March 7, 2008}}</ref> Scott is a dim-witted and lonely man, who attempts to win friends as the office comedian, usually making himself look bad in the process. 
* [[Rainn Wilson]] as [[Dwight Schrute]], who, based upon [[Gareth Keenan]], is the assistant to the regional manager, although the character frequently intentionally omits the "to the" in his title.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rooney|first=Brian|date=September 7, 2007|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Nightline/story?id=3566414&page=|title=The Man Behind 'The Office's' Favorite Suck-Up, Dwight Schrute|work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|access-date=March 7, 2008}}</ref> 
* [[John Krasinski]] as [[Jim Halpert]], a sales representative and prankster, who is based upon [[Tim Canterbury]], and has a crush on [[Pam Beesly]], the receptionist.<ref>{{cite web|last=Carter|first=Bill|date=March 20, 2005|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/03/20/arts/television/20Cart.html?pagewanted=2&_r=2&sq=John%20Krasinski&st=nyt&oref=slogin&scp=2&|title='The Office' Transfers to a New Cubicle|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=March 7, 2008}}</ref> 
* [[Jenna Fischer]] as [[Pam Beesly]], a [[receptionist]] based on [[Dawn Tinsley]], is shy, but is often a cohort with Jim in his pranks on Dwight.<ref>{{cite web|last=Stanley|first=Alessandra|date=March 24, 2005|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/03/24/arts/television/24stan.html?scp=1&sq=Jenna+Fischer&st=nyt|title=An American-Style 'Office' With a Boss From Heck|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=March 7, 2008}}</ref>
* [[B. J. Novak]] as [[Ryan Howard (The Office)|Ryan Howard]], a [[temporary worker]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Pesca|first=Mike|title=Talking With 'Office' Star B. J. Novak|url=https://www.npr.org/2008/05/12/90365876/talking-with-office-star-b-j-novak|access-date=May 31, 2022|publisher=[[NPR]]|date=May 12, 2008}}</ref>

==Broadcast and reception==

===Ratings===

{{image frame
|content={{#chart:OfficeUS1ratings.chart}}
|width = 500
|caption = Ratings for each episode of ''The Office'' that aired this season.{{ref|cite|i}}
}}

The first episode of ''The Office'' scored well in ratings, gaining over eleven million viewers, as well as ranking third in its timeslot on the night of its airing.<ref>{{cite web|last=Wilkes|first=Neil|date=March 26, 2005|url=http://www.digitalspy.com/tv/s155/the-office/news/a20222/american-office-an-early-ratings-hit.html|title=American 'Office' an Early Ratings Hit|work=[[Digital Spy]]|access-date=March 9, 2008}}</ref><ref name=boysngirls>{{cite web|last=Westbury|first=Anna|title=Infographic: The Lifespan of The Office|url=http://www.pastemagazine.com/blogs/1000words/2012/05/infographic-the-lifespan-of-the-office.html|publisher=[[Wolfgang's Vault]]|work=[[Paste Magazine]]|access-date=May 19, 2012|date=May 17, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120519134139/http://www.pastemagazine.com/blogs/1000words/2012/05/infographic-the-lifespan-of-the-office.html|archive-date=May 19, 2012}}</ref>  However the episode aired on a Thursday evening, and between the change from the first episode and the second episode, ''The Office'' moved to Tuesday evenings. ''The Office'' subsequently tumbled in the ratings, averaging under 6.0 million viewers, just over half that of the previous episode.<ref name=diversity>{{cite news|title=Nielsen Ratings Report: March 28–April 3, 2005|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-131972724.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171210231912/https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-131972724.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 10, 2017|access-date=January 5, 2013|newspaper=[[Variety (magazine)|Daily Variety]]|date=April 6, 2005}} {{subscription required}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Stunning Tumble for NBC's 'The Office'|url=http://www.medialifemagazine.com/News2005/mar05/mar28/3_wed/news1wednesday.html|newspaper=[[Media Life Magazine]]|access-date=June 20, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110520094347/http://www.medialifemagazine.com/News2005/mar05/mar28/3_wed/news1wednesday.html|archive-date=May 20, 2011|date=March 30, 2005}}</ref>  The first-season finale, "Hot Girl", received one of the lowest ratings in the show's history, earning just a 2.2 rating with a 10 share.<ref name=Low>{{cite news|title=Lower the Lights for NBC's 'The Office'|url=http://www.medialifemagazine.com/News2005/april05/apr25/3_wed/news2wednesday.html|newspaper=[[Media Life Magazine]]|access-date=June 20, 2012|archive-date=May 20, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110520094536/http://www.medialifemagazine.com/News2005/april05/apr25/3_wed/news2wednesday.html|date=April 27, 2005}}</ref> After the lackluster reception of the episode, many critics erroneously predicted that "Hot Girl" would also serve as the ''de facto'' [[series finale]].<ref name=Low/> ''The Office'' averaged 5.4 million viewers for its entire season, ranking it #102 for the 2004–2005 U.S. television season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr/television/feature_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1000937471|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080622125057/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/hr/search/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1000937471|archive-date=June 22, 2008|title=Final audience and ratings figures for 2004–05|newspaper=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=March 28, 2008}}</ref>

===Reviews===
[[File:Steve Carell November 2014.jpg|thumb|left|150px|[[Steve Carell]] was initially criticized for his portrayal of [[Michael Scott (The Office)|Michael Scott]], although his character soon garnered critical favor.|alt=A man with black hair, Steve Carell, is standing in a tux. He is looking towards the camera and smiles.]]

The series premiere, "Pilot", received largely mixed reviews from critics.<ref name="USDebut">{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/4375947.stm|title=''Office'' Remake Has its US TV debut|publisher=[[BBC]]|access-date=March 9, 2008}}</ref> After the first episodes, critics thought ''The Office'' would be another failed remake of a British comedy, much like how [[Coupling (American TV series)|the American version of ''Coupling'']] was in relation to [[Coupling (British TV series)|the original British series]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Maynard|first=John|date=March 20, 2005|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A37979-2005Mar15.html|title=''Office'' Humor and a Joyless 'Stick'|work=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=March 9, 2008}}</ref> ''The Deseret Morning News'' believed ''The Office'' was a failed remake, and said "Maybe, after ''The Office'' dies a quick death on NBC, the network will decide that trying to Americanize British TV comedies isn't such a great idea."<ref>{{cite web|last=Pierce|first=Scott|date=March 24, 2005|url=https://www.deseret.com/2005/3/24/19883486/nbc-is-off-target-with-the-office/|title=NBC Is Off Target with ''The Office''|work=[[Deseret News|The Deseret Morning News]]|access-date=March 9, 2008}}</ref> ''[[The New York Daily News]]'' said the show was "neither daring nor funny", adding that "NBC's version is so diluted there's little left but muddy water".<ref name=guardian/> ''[[The Los Angeles Times]]'' complained that [[Steve Carell]], who portrays Scott and also appeared in the movie ''[[Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy]]'', was "too cartoon" and said: "Lost in translation is the sadness behind the characters."<ref name=guardian>{{cite web|last=Gibson|first=Owen|date=March 23, 2005|url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2005/mar/24/usnews.broadcasting|title=US Version of Office Gets Cool Reception|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=February 23, 2008}}</ref>

Despite these criticisms, the remainder of the season earned mostly positive reviews among critics. The season as a whole scored 62 out of 100 on [[Metacritic]] (a website that assigns a weighted average score for media), which translates to "generally favorable" reviews.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.metacritic.com/tv/the-office/season-1 |title=The Office: Season 1 |publisher=[[Metacritic]] |access-date=July 14, 2013}}</ref> ''[[Time Magazine|Time]]'' magazine wrote that "It's ironic that NBC's most original sitcom in years is a remake, but who cares? ''The Office'' is a daring, unflinching take on very American workplace tensions."<ref name="USDebut"/> [[Boston.com]] felt that the first season of ''The Office'' was good, and the differences between the characters of the American and the original series added to the popularity of the series.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gilbert|first=Matthew|date=March 24, 2005|url=http://www.boston.com/ae/tv/articles/2005/03/24/the_office/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121018063555/http://www.boston.com/ae/tv/articles/2005/03/24/the_office/|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 18, 2012|title=It's Not as Warped as the Original, But 'The Office' is Painfully Funny|work=[[The Boston Globe]]|access-date=March 9, 2008}}</ref> Rob Owen of the ''[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]'' felt that ''The Office'' succeeded in its first season, and that although NBC had failed in the past with television shows such as ''Coupling'', it had found achievement with ''The Office''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Owen|first=Rob|date=March 23, 2005|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1129&dat=20050323&id=cYdIAAAAIBAJ&sjid=_XEDAAAAIBAJ&pg=5952,808377|title=TV Reviews: American 'Office' Works For and Gets the Laughs|work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|access-date=January 7, 2026}}</ref> ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' awarded the season a "B+" and wrote that ''The Office'' "is clever and insular, capturing all the drudgery, awkwardness, and rivalry of cubicle living" and that the last five episodes help to illustrate that the series has "crossed the pond handily."<ref>{{cite web|last=Flynn|first=Gillian|date=March 15, 2005|url=http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,1037072,00.html|title=''The Office''|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080213103556/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,1037072,00.html|archive-date=February 13, 2008|work=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|url-status=dead|access-date=February 11, 2008}}</ref>

===Accolades===
In its first year, ''The Office'' was nominated for several awards, including three [[Writers Guild of America Award]] nods. These included nominations for [[Writers Guild of America Award for Best Screenplay – Comedy Series|Best Comedy Series]] and [[Writers Guild of America Award for Best Screenplay – New Series|Best New Series]]. For his work on "Diversity Day", [[B. J. Novak]] was also nominated for [[Writers Guild of America Award for Best Screenplay – Episodic Comedy|Best Screenplay – Episodic Comedy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wga.org/subpage_newsevents.aspx?id=1493|title=2006 Writers Guild Awards Television and Radio Nominees Announced|publisher=[[Writers Guild of America]]|date=December 14, 2005|access-date=December 24, 2025|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120525050001/http://www.wga.org/subpage_newsevents.aspx?id=1493|archive-date=May 25, 2012}}</ref>

Dwight's chosen plan slashes benefits, much to the chagrin of the other employees.  In an attempt to appease them, Michael promises the entire office a surprise, and then spends the rest of the day scrambling to come through with his promise. The employees wait for Michael's surprise, which he awkwardly never delivers. Meanwhile, Jim and Pam amuse themselves with Dwight's medical forms.
 |LineColor = fff777
}}

== DVD release ==
The first season of ''The Office'' was released by Universal Studios Home Entertainment as a single-disc Region 1 DVD set on August 16, 2005.<ref>{{cite web |author=Lacey, Gord |date=June 1, 2005 |url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Office/3478 |title=Head to "''The Office'' This Summer |publisher=TV Shows On DVD|access-date=March 10, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080204031114/http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Office/3478 |archive-date=February 4, 2008 }}</ref> The set includes all 6 episodes presented in a 1.78:1 aspect ratio with Dolby Digital 2.0 Stereo sound and optional English and Spanish subtitles. The release also included audio commentaries for 4 episodes, as well as deleted scenes from every episode.<ref name="DVD4">{{cite AV media notes |title=The Office: The Complete First Season |last=Kwapis|first=Ken|type=DVD |publisher=[[Universal Television|Universal]] |location=[[Los Angeles]]|display-authors=etal}}</ref>

== Explanatory notes ==
{{note|a|i}} Toby Huss provided Todd Packer's voice in "Pilot". In subsequent episodes, the character would be played by [[David Koechner]].<ref name=mashable-cite>{{cite web |url=https://mashable.com/article/the-office-ladies-podcast/ |title=Why the 'Office Ladies' podcast is worth your time |website=[[Mashable]] |first=Nicole |last=Gallucci |date=October 16, 2019 |access-date=October 22, 2019}}</ref><br/>
